items.title: Mentors’ Perspectives on Supporting Newly Graduated Registered Nurses in Hospital Settings: A Qualitative Focus Group Study
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Research consistently highlights the importance of mentorship and a supportive work environment for newly graduated registered nurses entering clinical settings. Previous research on mentorship has primarily focused on new nurses' perspectives. Further research is needed to explore mentors' perspectives in greater depth. Aim To explore mentors' perspectives on supporting newly graduated registered nurses in their professional development in a hospital setting. Design The study had a qualitative explorative design using focus group discussions as a data collection method. Method A total of 18 registered nurses serving as mentors in a hospital care unit participated in five focus group discussions. The data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings The findings revealed mentors' views that a permissive approach, creating a trusting relationship, and strengthening self‐confidence build a positive foundation for novice nurses. They wished to facilitate novice nurses' learning towards professional independence by encouraging reflection and probing, and by fostering a desire for ongoing clinical competence development and patient safety through their presence in daily practice. Conclusion These findings underscore the crucial role of mentors as advanced nurses in fostering supportive learning environments for newly graduated registered nurses by establishing meaningful mentoring relationships that offer psychological support. Extending existing mentor literature, the results highlight their intention to deliver pedagogically grounded, hands‐on clinical mentorship integrated into daily practice to ensure patient care. Thereby fostering workplace learning and professional development in daily clinical practice. Implications for the Profession Health care decision‐makers and managers could use knowledge gained from this study to implement more targeted mentorship programmes to support newly graduated registered nurses and promote workplace learning. The findings emphasise the importance of organisational support, including protected time for mentors, to sustain meaningful mentorship and promote nurses' well‐being and healthy work environments. Impact: (Addressing) What problem did the study address? Mentorship plays a critical role in supporting newly graduated registered nurses entering clinical settings. However, despite the recognised importance of mentorship, there is limited research exploring mentors' perspectives when supporting new nurses. What were the main findings? Mentors can build a positive foundation for newly graduated registered nurses by using a permissive approach to create a trusting relationship. Mentors' intention was to promote a pedagogically grounded learning environment and uphold knowledge support through being present in daily work in order to create security for new nurses and ensure patient care. Where and on whom will the research have an impact? The findings of this study may support mentors and nurse managers responsible for facilitating the transition of newly graduated registered nurses into hospital settings by informing mentorship approaches that promote professional development through workplace learning and foster psychological safety during the transition period. Additionally, effective mentorship may strengthen newly graduated registered nurses' ability to deliver high‐quality care, which is of particular interest to nurse managers seeking to ensure safe and effective patient care. Reporting Method This study conforms to the reporting of the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research guidelines and checklist. No Patient or Public Involvement This study did not include patient or public involvement in its design, conduct, or reporting.

items.title: Microplastics and the Kidney: A Narrative Review of Human Evidence, Molecular Mechanisms of Cell Injury, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are widespread environmental contaminants, but their potential effects on kidney health remain poorly defined. As an organ continuously exposed to circulating particles and involved in their urinary elimination, the kidney may represent both a target of MP toxicity and a route of excretion. In this narrative review, we examine current evidence linking MPs to kidney injury, integrating experimental, mechanistic, and human data. Particular attention is given to the early events governing particle–cell interactions. After exposure, micro- and nanoplastics acquire an eco- and biomolecular corona that modifies their surface properties, cellular recognition, uptake, and biodistribution. Following internalization through phagocytic and endocytic pathways, particles may accumulate within endolysosomal compartments and interact with intracellular structures, disrupting cellular homeostasis. In renal cells, these events converge on mitochondrial dysfunction, reactive oxygen species generation, endoplasmic reticulum stress, inflammatory signaling, altered autophagy, and regulated cell death. Several interconnected pathways have been implicated, including Keap1–Nrf2/ARE and NF-κB signaling, MAPK and IRE1/XBP1-mediated stress responses, ACSL4–GPX4-related ferroptosis, and TGF-β1-related profibrotic signaling. Human studies have detected MPs in urine and kidney tissue and provide preliminary evidence linking MP burden with early markers of kidney damage, although current findings remain limited by small study populations and substantial methodological heterogeneity. Patients with chronic kidney disease, particularly those receiving dialysis, may represent a population of special interest because potentially altered renal handling may coexist with repeated exposure to polymer-based medical devices and dialysis fluids. Despite this potential relevance, data on MP exposure and accumulation in CKD and dialysis patients remain remarkably scarce. We finally discuss the limitations of current experimental models and analytical methods and the need for standardized biomonitoring, more environmentally relevant particles and exposure concentrations, and detection strategies capable of reaching the nanoscale, including artificial intelligence-assisted analysis. Overall, available evidence provides a mechanistic basis for MP-induced kidney injury, but its clinical relevance and contribution to human kidney disease remain to be established.

items.abstract: Teacher work motivation and group dynamics are essential in supporting educational quality. Teachers often face challenges such as heavy workloads, limited facilities, administrative demands, and personal differences that affect motivation, communication, and collaboration. This article explores Sharia-based values as an approach to strengthening teacher motivation and group dynamics in Islamic educational institutions. Using a descriptive qualitative literature review, the study examines recent publications on work motivation, group dynamics, Islamic leadership, and Sharia values. Findings show that values of ikhlas (sincerity), amanah (trustworthiness), ihsan (excellence), ta’awun (mutual assistance), ukhuwah (brotherhood), and syura (consultation) strengthen intrinsic motivation, professional responsibility, mutual support, effective communication, and collaborative relationships among teachers. Islamic leadership plays a key role in translating these values into practice through fairness, exemplary conduct, participation, and open communication. Integrating Sharia values into school management provides a foundation for enhancing professionalism, cooperation, positive group dynamics, and a supportive work environment, ultimately improving educational quality.

items.title: Motivation, work, and mobility: developing a process framework of employee turnover intentions in Indian nonprofits
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the mechanisms associated with employees’ turnover intentions in Indian non-profit organisations (NPOs). Existing employee turnover research provides limited understanding of how individual, organisational, and sector-level dynamics relate to turnover intentions in Indian NPOs. To address this gap, the study aims to develop a process-orientated framework grounded in employees' lived experiences. Design/methodology/approach This study adopted a qualitative approach using semi-structured interviews with 17 non-profit employees, managers, leaders, and sector stakeholders. Participants were purposively selected to capture diverse organisational roles and sector experiences. Data were analysed using the Gioia methodology. Findings The analysis develops a process framework comprising five interconnected dimensions: mission attachment spectrum, employment deal and financial viability, work design and career trajectories, leadership and organisational culture, and development-sector labour-market dynamics. Together, these dimensions describe how employees evaluate their employment conditions, interpret their relationship with the organisational mission, and respond to opportunities in the broader development-sector labour-market. Originality/value This study contributes a process-orientated framework of employee turnover intentions, advancing four theoretical propositions grounded in qualitative evidence from the Indian non-profit sector. The framework extends the employee turnover literature by integrating individual, organisational, and sector-level dynamics into a contextual explanation of employee turnover intentions in Indian NPOs. The framework illustrates how turnover intentions may emerge through the interaction of mission attachment, organisational conditions, and development-sector labour-market dynamics over time. These insights may have relevance not only to Indian NPOs but also to NPOs operating in other resource-constrained and emerging economy contexts.

items.title: Multimodal Trust Assessment in Human–AI Shared Control Systems
items.abstract: Trust plays an important role in human–AI shared-control systems, yet it is difficult to assess from a single observable signal. This study proposes an event-centered multimodal framework for assessing situational trust by integrating contextual, behavioral, affective, and individual features surrounding critical human–AI interaction events. A controlled autonomous-driving experiment was conducted with 15 participants under high- and low-reliability conditions, yielding 117 valid event-level observations with retrospective trust ratings. The results showed substantial differences in reported trust between reliability conditions and across failure types, while facial and failure-related contextual indicators were among the more informative variables. However, the highly imbalanced trust classes, particularly the limited number of high-trust observations, constrained reliable classification of individual trust levels. The findings only provide preliminary evidence that event-level multimodal observations can characterize information associated with reported situational trust, while also demonstrating the challenges of cross-user trust estimation under limited and imbalanced data. Therefore, the study serves as a methodological and empirical starting point for developing more robust multimodal trust assessment approaches, rather than as a validation of a generalized real-time trust prediction system.

items.title: NAVIGATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND RELIGIOUS AUTHORITY IN NIGERIA: RECONFIGURING RELIGIOUS KNOWLEDGE, LEADERSHIP AND TRUST IN THE DIGITAL AGE
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly becoming part of religious education, communication, research and everyday faith practices. Believers can now use generative AI to explain sacred texts, compare interpretations, prepare devotional materials and seek answers to religious questions without first consulting a recognised religious leader. This development raises an important question for Nigeria: how is religious authority changing when access to religious information is no longer controlled mainly by clergy, scholars and religious institutions? This paper examines the relationship between AI and religious authority in Nigeria, focusing on religious knowledge, leadership and trust. Using a conceptual and interpretive methodology, it synthesises scholarship on religious authority, digital religion, AI ethics and Nigerian religious experience. It argues that AI is not simply replacing religious authorities; rather, it is reconfiguring the conditions under which authority is produced, accessed, evaluated and trusted. Nigerian digital-religion research shows that digital infrastructures can create new forms of religious influence and authority, while recent AI scholarship highlights concerns about accuracy, privacy, bias and human accountability. The paper proposes a Responsible Religious AI Engagement Framework based on human accountability, verification, contextual sensitivity, confidentiality and formation. It concludes that Nigerian religious institutions should neither reject AI nor surrender religious judgment to it. AI should remain an assistive instrument while theological discernment, pastoral responsibility, communal recognition and human dignity remain central to religious leadership.

items.title: Noncommutative Cultural Dynamics: A Unified State-Space Framework for Weakly and Strongly Correlated Cultural Fields
items.abstract: This project develops a unified mathematical and computational framework for cultural dynamics based on noncommutative operators, state-space modeling, and multi-scale correlation structures. Cultural change is represented as the evolution of latent cultural fields that may be weakly correlated (ancient and pre-modern societies) or strongly correlated (modern media-driven environments). The model integrates continuous-time dynamics, discrete noncommutative transitions, generational eigenmodes, and media-induced perturbations. The framework is extended across multiple structural layers: (1) network-based cultural diffusion using graph Laplacians, (2) spatial cultural propagation via partial differential equations, (3) AI-based implementations including neural ODEs, graph neural networks, physics-informed neural networks, and diffusion models, (4) optimal control formulations for policy intervention, (5) evolutionary game-theoretic cultural adaptation, (6) general-equilibrium economic integration, and (7) narrative-field modeling for story generation and cultural feedback. Together, these components form a comprehensive “Unified Cultural Field Theory” that connects cultural sociology, cognitive science, AI theory, narrative studies, economics, and noncommutative geometry. The project situates cultural dynamics within a rigorous mathematical structure while enabling practical applications in media analysis, trend forecasting, policy design, and generative AI.

items.title: Outcomes-Based Independent Learning Paradigm (OBILP): Effects on Students' Engagement and Performance in Chemistry
items.abstract: This study investigated the effects of the Outcomes-Based Independent Learning Paradigm (OBILP) on Grade 10 students’ engagement and performance in chemistry, focusing on the domains of gas laws, biomolecules, and chemical equations and reactions. An Explanatory Sequential Mixed-Methods design was employed. The quantitative phase utilized a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control group design involving Grade 10 students from Bacayawan National High School during the school year 2022–2023. Results indicated that both control and experimental groups exhibited very high levels of affective engagement and high levels of behavioral and cognitive engagement, with no significant differences across the three components. However, the experimental group achieved significantly higher mean scores (p = 0.010) and mean gain scores (p = 0.035) than the control group. No significant correlation was found between students’ engagement and performance before and after the intervention. The qualitative phase, through interviews and student journal entries, provided explanatory insights into these findings, revealing that OBILP enhanced student engagement and performance, while chemical reactions and equations remained the most challenging topic domain. These results suggest that OBILP has the potential to improve chemistry learning outcomes, although future studies should employ larger samples and broader contexts to strengthen generalizability.

items.title: PandemIQ system in Poland: The hybrid approach to early detection of pandemic waves using interpretable AI models and GIS-based operational dashboards (ArcGIS)
items.abstract: Humans live surrounded by a variety of threats. These threats can be diverse: natural, chemical, technological, psychological, social, ecological, global, biological, and health-related. The latter, namely biological and health threats, are the most pressing and dangerous from a human perspective as they affect living organisms’ health. Examples include infectious diseases caused by viruses, bacteria, or parasites (e.g., influenza, COVID-19, Lyme disease). In Poland, epidemic cases of the acute infectious respiratory disease COVID-19, caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, were first reported on March 4, 2020. The pandemic lasted three years. This scientific article attempts to present the architecture and functionality of the PandemIQ system. The system was designed for the early detection and forecasting of the regional risk of pandemic waves. The system is based on a hybrid artificial intelligence model that combines predictions based on epidemiological, mobility, and transportation data with interpretability (attention) mechanisms enabling visualization and decision justification. This paper provides a detailed discussion of the structure of decision reports for authorities, GIS-based operational dashboards (ArcGIS), and alternative solutions using the Apache ECharts library. It also presents validation procedures, data security aspects, and compliance with legal regulations (GDPR, AI Act). Simulation results using historical data on the spread of the SARS-CoV-2 virus indicate that the system can detect waves on average 7–14 days earlier than traditional epidemiological methods can, while maintaining a low false alarm rate.

items.title: Parallel science and technology for C2 in the agentic age: from military operations to peaceful sustainability and resiliency
items.abstract: Abstract Command and control (C2) has traditionally been framed as a military problem of sensing, deciding, coordinating, and acting under uncertainty, conflict, and time pressure. In the agentic age, however, this problem is being extended far beyond the battlefield, as human organizations become increasingly embedded in hybrid environments composed of artificial agents, digital twins, social sensing networks, foundation models, autonomous platforms, and cyber–physical–social institutions. This article develops a conceptual framework for parallel science and technology for C2 by revisiting the historical mission of C2 as a quest for certainty under diversity, uncertainty, and complexity (DUC), and by tracing its transformation toward focus, agility, and convergence (FAC). Building on parallel systems, artificial societies, computational experiments, parallel execution (ACP), cyber–physical–social systems (CPSS), C2 management (C2M), planning–readiness–execution–assessment (PREA) loops, social cognition operations, and parallel battlefield intelligence, the article argues that C2 should be reframed as a general science of coordinated adaptation. It further examines emerging agentic societies as a new operating ecology, explains why parallel science and technology are needed, and redefines the mission of future C2 around sustainability and resiliency. Rather than merely accelerating decision cycles or optimizing combat efficiency, parallel C2 aims to support anticipation, adaptation, trust, recovery, and responsible human agency across both military and civilian domains, thereby transforming command and control from post-hoc operational control into a science of sustainable and resilient coordination in the agentic age.

items.title: Partnering With Generative Artificial Intelligence for Quantitative Data Analysis in Nursing Research: A Practical Workflow for Ethical Collaboration
items.abstract: Reproducibility and replicability are our scientific and ethical mandate, and the foundation of trust in nursing science and research. Both rest on transparent documentation of how data were actually analyzed. The rising use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in research intersects with this mandate, with the potential to either support or undermine it, yet practical guidance for conducting GenAI-assisted quantitative analysis remains limited. This gap is particularly relevant for nurse scientists, who increasingly work with complex, biologically-informed datasets spanning genomics, symptoms, and patient outcomes. To address this gap, we present a practice-based guide for partnering with GenAI in quantitative data analysis in nursing research, grounded in a nursing-focused genomic research example. We cover GenAI literacy spanning three dimensions (technical, practical, and ethical) and a two-phase workflow for human-GenAI collaboration spanning planning and pre-specification through code development, formal analysis, translation, and human review and disclosure of GenAI use. The core principle is using GenAI as a tool, not a decision-maker, as scientific integrity requires that humans retain interpretive authority. We further propose a synthetic-data-first approach as a privacy safeguard. We illustrate these concepts through a genetics example, though the principles and workflow generalize to many quantitative nursing research contexts.

items.title: PawSense_AI Assistant
items.abstract: The increasing adoption of artificial intelligence in everyday applications has created opportunities to improve access to pet-care information and support pet owners in making informed decisions about animal health and well-being. This paper presents PawSense AI, an AI-powered pet-care assistance system designed to provide accessible, interactive, and personalized support to pet owners through a web-based platform. The proposed system integrates generative artificial intelligence, image-based pet assessment, voice interaction, and location-based veterinary search within a unified interface. Users can interact with the system through natural-language queries, upload pet images for preliminary AI-assisted observations, and access information about nearby veterinary facilities. The application incorporates user authentication and database-supported conversation management to maintain individual accounts and chat histories. Voice transcription and multilingual response options further aim to improve accessibility and ease of interaction. The system is developed using Python and the Flask web framework, with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the user interface, database technologies for information management, and external AI and mapping services for intelligent responses and location-based information. PawSense AI is intended to complement existing pet-care resources by providing convenient access to general guidance and helping users identify relevant veterinary services. However, AI-generated observations are not a substitute for professional veterinary diagnosis, and the reliability of the system depends on the underlying AI models, external services, and input quality. The proposed platform demonstrates an integrated approach to AI-assisted pet-care information access, with potential for further development through systematic evaluation, improved personalization, and expanded multilingual capabilities. Keywords— PawSense AI, Artificial Intelligence, Pet Care, Generative AI, Image Analysis, Voice Assistant, Veterinary Services, Flask Web Application.

items.title: Paying for Nutrition: A Mechanism-Design Approach to the Nutrient Density Standard
items.abstract: Can a voluntary farm-gate payment improve the nutritional quality of food crops at a defensible cost? This paper proposes a Nutrient Density Bonus for verified protein, zinc, and iron in harvested wheat, alongside existing income protection. It compares three payment architectures: direct lot assays, contracts for specified practices, and evidence-backed claims subject to independent audits. A capped, volume-adjusted payment rule makes the unit of reward explicit; a simplified deterrence condition identifies the recovery and enforcement assumptions behind the audit mechanism. The proposed evaluation begins with a measurement season in western Kansas and northern Oklahoma, followed, only if feasible, by a controlled comparison over multiple harvests. Reference assays remain the basis for mineral verification unless predictive methods meet prespecified payment-relevant error tolerances. The policy must demonstrate additional crop-quality improvement, affordable verification, fair access, and acceptable effects on yield, income, food safety, and the environment. Higher grain mineral concentration is distinguished from nutrient output, bioavailability, and health benefit. The contribution is a policy-design framework and prospective evaluation plan; no pilot results or national cost estimate are reported. Status: Policy working paper, version 1.0; not peer reviewed. No new dataset, completed pilot, or national cost estimate is reported. Provenance: A revised archival adaptation of the June 2026 web proposal. items.abstract: This thesis investigates the structured integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools within higher pedagogical education under specialty 13.00.01. As educational paradigms shift globally towards digital environments, future educators must develop comprehensive digital-pedagogical competencies. The study highlights the key technical, methodological, and psychological conditions necessary to successfully adapt generative AI systems like large language models and smart tutoring agents in training workflows. Ultimately, the paper proposes a cohesive pedagogical framework aimed at boosting critical thinking and lesson planning efficiency among upcoming school teachers.

items.title: Pedagogical Foundations of Active Learning: Rethinking Teaching Approaches for the Next Generation of Educators
items.abstract: Active learning is widely promoted to enhance learner participation and meaningful learning, yet its conceptualization remains fragmented across instructional techniques, engagement processes, teacher roles, and emerging technological contexts. This conceptual article reconsiders active learning as a coherent pedagogical orientation and develops an integrative account of its pedagogical foundations for the next generation of educators. Drawing on a thematic synthesis of relevant literature, the article identifies interconnected dimensions comprising pedagogical purpose, meaningful learning activity, cognitive engagement, teacher facilitation, learner agency, feedback, relational conditions, and digital/AI environments. The synthesis positions cognitive engagement as a central mechanism through which purposeful activities contribute to meaningful learning, while teacher facilitation and learning conditions sustain this process. The resulting framework conceptualizes active learning as a dynamic, interdependent, and recursive pedagogical system, rather than a linear sequence or collection of techniques. Digital and AI technologies are positioned as contextual pedagogical affordances whose value depends on purposeful integration and critical use. The framework repositions teachers as pedagogical designers and facilitators who orchestrate learning conditions while sustaining learner agency. This conceptualization provides a coherent foundation for understanding active learning and preparing educators to design meaningful, learner-centered environments responsive to contemporary educational demands.

items.abstract: Audited interim result, not completed PENTA certification. Four platform-configured engines were observed in two fresh web conversations each with memory disabled, using a frozen six-case synthetic decision prompt. Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol matched the registered canonical JSON tuple hash in both recorded captures. GPT-5.6 Luna matched in A but differed in B. GLM 5.2 replayed consistently but differed from the registered target in both captures. DeepSeek has not been captured. All 48 recorded decisions selected the expected playbook name and id. Full registered tuple equality held for 30/48 decisions. The remaining 18 differed only in spaces inside the steps_executed string. Pretty-printing outside strings is removed by canonicalization and is not a failure cause. The prompt's lack of an explicit space delimiter contract is disclosed; failures remain failures against the preregistered target. Limitations: UI-transcribed rendered captures, not raw provider responses; model attribution by Base44 configuration, not backend attestation; supplementary fresh-chat method deviates from original same-conversation registration; shared instructions, workspace and expected answers remain available; Sol executed skills in both captures; Opus A conversation attribution was inferred from sidebar/timestamp ordering. This is not a stress/load test, live-healing test, general governance certification, or proof of runtime enforcement. Confidence-hold and no-match branches were not exercised. Audit and correction: earlier copied Luna files and single-turn Opus/Sol attempts are excluded, preserved, and labeled. Earlier operator claims of raw byte-exactness and 100% governance are corrected explicitly. Deterministic Phase A/C receipts are harness-computed, not LLM inference evidence. No failure is normalized into a pass. Dual Mesh Benchmark: not measured in this experiment. No comparative mesh, latency, learning or healing performance claim is made. Bundle contains the technical note in PDF/Markdown, machine-readable receipt, full evidence archive, offline verifier, original preregistration, excluded attempts, and SHA-256 manifest. All test data is synthetic. AI assistance and capture provenance are disclosed. Registration: public commit deadfea. Results: GitHub evidence. Research home: DCAI; portal: DSOS Science. Lineage acknowledged: Nyquist, Hartley, Shannon, Kolmogorov. No new mechanism is claimed. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects on them.

items.title: Performance Limitations of Large Language Models in Processing Low-Resource Regional Languages: Empirical Evidence and Pre-Training Optimization Strategies
items.abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT and Gemini have transformed information processing in resource-rich languages, their effectiveness significantly diminishes when applied to low-resource regional languages (e.g., Sundanese and Javanese). This paper investigates the performance bottlenecks experienced by users, focusing on latency and output fluency. Through a quantitative survey (N = 50), we argue that these limitations stem from underrepresentation during the model pre-training phase and inefficient tokenization. Consequently, we propose prioritizing vocabulary expansion and open-source regional corpus collection during the pre-training stage to enhance AI inclusivity and fluency.

items.title: Physically inspired geometry-to-photometry rendering and lightweight convolutional neural network for real-time weld defect detection
items.abstract: Welding quality inspection of battery top covers is critical to lithium-ion battery safety and reliability. The height deviation between weld defects and normal areas is extremely small; on specular, weakly textured surfaces it produces no stable brightness contrast, so two-dimensional (2D) images carry almost no usable defect signal. Three-dimensional (3D) sensing captures such deviations but incurs computational costs prohibitive for production lines. Raw depth maps, as scalar grayscale fields, cause 2D convolutional networks to overlook tiny-defect features. Addressing all three limitations simultaneously remains a key challenge for artificial intelligence (AI) in industrial inspection. To address this challenge, we propose a geometry-to-photometry defect detection framework that converts 3D weld geometry into discriminative 2D photometric representations via physically inspired rendering. Depth data are first mapped to pseudo-color images, and surface normals then modulate lighting under a Phong-based model to transform subtle geometric discontinuities into high-contrast photometric cues. Building on this strategy, we develop YOLO-WaveletTiny (YOLO-WT), a lightweight You Only Look Once (YOLO) detector integrating wavelet depthwise separable convolution and inverse wavelet upsampling for efficient feature extraction and reconstruction. Experiments on a real industrial dataset with six defect categories show the rendered representation improves the baseline by 5.9 percentage points in mean average precision at 50% intersection over union (mAP@50), and the full framework achieves 93.8% mAP@50 with only 2.47 million parameters and 5.7 GFLOPs, outperforming mainstream detectors. These results demonstrate the framework as an effective, practical AI solution for low-cost, high-precision weld defect inspection.

items.title: Predicting Lentil Seed Yield from Agronomic Traits Using a Foundation-Augmented Machine Learning Ensemble
items.abstract: Accurate agricultural yield prediction is crucial for crop management and data-driven decision-making. This study proposes a machine learning framework for predicting total lentil seed yield using 264 observations collected during a single growing season at one location in Sivas, Türkiye. Seven regression models and the tabular foundation model TabPFN were evaluated through nested cross-validation. The fixed post hoc Foundation-Augmented Averaging Ensemble (FAAE) combined TabPFN, Extra Trees, CatBoost, and XGBoost using equal weights, while the primary fully nested evaluation selected the four ensemble members within each outer training fold. The fully nested FAAE achieved R2 = 0.891 ± 0.045, comparable to the strongest individual models, while the fixed post hoc FAAE yielded R2 = 0.897 ± 0.038. Split conformal prediction produced well-calibrated uncertainty intervals at 80%, 90%, and 95% coverage. SHAP and LOCO identified pods per plant and biological yield as the dominant predictors of lentil yield. Overall, these findings indicate that FAAE can provide competitive predictive performance within a leakage-controlled framework while also supporting uncertainty quantification and biologically meaningful interpretation. Because the dominant predictors, pods per plant and biological yield, are measured at or near physiological maturity, the proposed framework is more suitable for end-of-season yield estimation than for early-season forecasting. The framework therefore shows potential for within-trial yield assessment, although validation using replicated material across additional years and locations is required before broader generalization.

items.title: Predictive Policing dan Negara Hukum: Analisis Yuridis Penggunaan Artificial Intelligence dalam Pencegahan Kejahatan di Indonesia
items.abstract: Predictive policing based on artificial intelligence is shifting crime prevention from reactive response toward data-driven risk identification, pattern recognition, and resource prioritization. This transformation creates a legal dilemma: the same systems that may improve analytical capacity can also amplify historical bias, enable opaque profiling, intrude upon privacy, and influence coercive decisions without adequate procedural safeguards. This article analyzes the legal position of predictive policing in Indonesia and formulates a rights-based governance model for police use of artificial intelligence. The research applies normative juridical analysis using statutory, conceptual, comparative, and policy approaches. The analysis focuses on the 2022 Personal Data Protection Law, the 2023 Criminal Code, the 2025 Criminal Procedure Code, the 2026 amendment to the Police Law, and Indonesia's emerging national AI governance framework. The study finds that Indonesia already possesses fragmented legal bases relevant to AI-supported policing, but lacks a dedicated risk-based framework that defines prohibited uses, high-risk systems, human oversight, auditability, contestability, and allocation of responsibility. The article proposes a four-layer governance model: constitutional safeguards, statutory legality, AI governance controls, and operational human review. Predictive outputs should function as decision-support rather than autonomous grounds for coercive action.

items.title: Prevalence of vocal discomfort among primary school teachers at selected schools.
items.abstract: Introduction:Teachers form the backbone of any educational system, shaping future generations through constant interaction and communication.In the Indian context, where classroom resources are often limited, the teacher's voice becomes the most vital instructional tool.However, prolonged and excessive voice use places teachers at considerable risk of vocal discomfort, presenting as dryness, hoarseness, throat irritation, and voice fatigue.These symptoms not only hinder effective teaching but also affect teachers' well-being, productivity, and overall quality of education.Despite its significance, vocal health remains a largely overlooked occupational concern among school teachers, particularly at the primary level.Recognizing this gap, the present study was undertaken to explore the magnitude of vocal discomfort among primary school teachers.Material and method A non-experimental descriptive research design was adopted for the study.A total of 200 primary school teachers from selected schools in the Sangli-Miraj-Kupwad Corporation area were included using a cluster sampling technique.Data was collected using the standardized Vocal Tract Discomfort Scale (VTDS) developed by Mathieson, administered in both Marathi and English for better comprehension.The tool comprised two sections: demographic variables and an 8-item self-rating scale assessing frequency and severity of vocal discomfort symptoms on a 6-point Likert scale.The total score ranged from 0 to 96 and was categorized into no, normal, mild, moderate, and extreme levels of vocal discomfort.Content validity was established by 20 experts, ensuring the tool's appropriateness for the study setting. Results:The findings revealed a notable burden of vocal discomfort among teachers.Symptoms such as dryness (46%), aching (43.5%), and soreness (39.5%) were commonly reported, followed by tightness (34%) and burning sensations (31.5%).Overall, most participants experienced mild (65%) to moderate (35%) levels of discomfort.The prevalence of vocal discomfort was found to be 45.56%.Female teachers constituted a larger proportion of the sample, and most participants had 1-10 years of teaching experience, with an average daily teaching duration of 5-6 hours. Conclusion:The study highlights that nearly half of the primary school teachers experience some degree of vocal discomfort, underscoring it as a significant occupational health issue.Although vocal discomfort appears to be influenced by demographic and work-related factors, no statistically significant association was observed in this study.These findings emphasize the need for early screening, awareness programs, and preventive voice care strategies to safeguard teachers' vocal health and enhance their professional efficiency.

items.title: Prioritising substances of concern for monitoring by using knowledge graphs and public datasets
items.abstract: Abstract Air pollution is identified by the World Health Organisation (WHO) as the leading environmental threat to human health, with indoor exposure particularly concerning given its daily, long-term nature. Europeans spend approximately 90% of their time indoors, where poor indoor air quality (IAQ) contributes an estimated 2 million disability-adjusted life-years lost annually in the EU, with vulnerable populations especially at risk. This study explores a Knowledge Graph (KG) as a decision-support tool to prioritise Substances of Concern (SoC) for indoor dust and air. Two complementary approaches were applied: a top-down screening that filters a broad substance universe against defined criteria to identify monitoring candidates, and a bottom-up characterisation of already monitored substances against the same criteria. Integrating publicly available chemical data within the KG and applying a risk-oriented approach based on hazard classification, REACH registration tonnage and use information, we narrowed a list of over 16,000 substances (PlastChem list) down to 42. This work shows that KG can effectively connect diverse data sources and identified both known and emerging SoC not yet monitored in private settings. It highlights that non-REACH chemicals may contribute significantly to indoor dust chemistry analysis, and REACH consumer-use data alone does not capture all uses relevant to residential indoor exposure. The experiments show that expanding the number and diversity of integrated data sources is recommended to refine scoping for chemical monitoring, risk assessment and management. Key concerns among identified substances include reproductive toxicity and respiratory tract irritation, often linked to numerous consumer products. The ECHA Classification and Labelling Inventory was found to be a useful hazardous substance pool, though further refinement with additional health-related data is recommended. Finally, we discuss how integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) and KG into the framework could support partial automation of the validation of SoC, improving future monitoring and analysis efficiency.

items.title: RECURSIVE STRUCTURAL REALITY: A FOUNDATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR REALITY, RECURSION, AND THE REFLECTIVE OBSERVER
items.abstract: Human inquiry has developed through philosophy, mathematics, physics, biology, logic, psychology, cognitive science, religious studies, and numerous other disciplines. Each investigates particular aspects of existence through its own concepts, methods, and standards of explanation. Yet the relationships among these domains raise a fundamental question: Can a common structural framework help us understand how different forms of organisation emerge, persist, transform, and become intelligible to observers within reality? Recursive Structural Reality (RSR) proposes such a framework through the interconnected concepts of existence, difference, relation, structure, information, transformation, recursion, stability, persistence, and identity. Its central proposition, Identity = Stable Recursion, directs attention towards the processes through which recognisable organisation may persist despite changes in components, states, or circumstances. RSR also investigates the conditions under which structures lose stability, undergo transformation, reorganise, and give rise to new forms of organisation. A second foundational dimension concerns the observer. Human beings do not investigate reality from outside the universe but participate in the reality they seek to understand. Through perception, memory, language, logic, mathematics, and reflection, observers construct models that organise experience and make particular aspects of existence intelligible. These models are indispensable to knowledge, yet they remain selective representations whose assumptions, limitations, and domains of validity require examination. The scope of RSR extends from foundational ontology and mathematical structures to physical systems, biological organisation, intelligence, artificial intelligence, consciousness, knowledge, religious traditions, and social institutions. These domains provide different contexts in which questions about structure, transformation, stability, persistence, and identity can be investigated. Their inclusion within a common framework does not imply that they share identical mechanisms or can be explained through one undifferentiated model. Each application requires concepts, methods, and standards of evidence appropriate to its subject. RSR therefore distinguishes philosophical RSR, mathematical RSR, and physical RSR while situating them within a broader interdisciplinary research programme. Philosophical coherence, mathematical derivation, and physical validity are related but distinct requirements. Similarly, applications to biological, cognitive, religious, and social phenomena require their own explanatory development and appropriate forms of investigation. This paper establishes the conceptual foundations, expanded scope, methodological orientation, and research architecture of RSR. It presents the framework as an evolving programme whose contributions must be assessed through conceptual precision, formal development, explanatory value, and empirical or comparative investigation. Its long-term objective is an integrated understanding of reality that investigates structural connections across domains without erasing their differences, while examining both the phenomena under investigation and the limitations of the models through which they are understood.

items.title: Reimagining entrepreneurship in the age of generative AI: the mediating role of innovation
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how three dimensions of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), namely, capability, application and knowledge modelling, are associated with entrepreneurial innovation, and whether innovation mediates their associations with entrepreneurial performance and entrepreneurial success in startups and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 317 startup and SME owners, partners and employees were analysed using confirmatory factor analysis followed by AMOS-based structural path analysis in IBM SPSS analysis of moment structures (AMOS) 20.0 with maximum likelihood estimation. Specific indirect effects were assessed using bias-corrected bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples and 95% confidence intervals. Findings All three GenAI dimensions were positively associated with entrepreneurial innovation, with knowledge modelling showing the largest reported association. Entrepreneurial innovation was positively associated with performance and success, and all six specific indirect associations were significant. The largest reported indirect associations were observed for knowledge modelling. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional, single-source design supports associations rather than causal claims. Practical implications Entrepreneurs should prioritise knowledge-related practices, verification of AI-generated information and human judgement rather than treating tool use alone as evidence of innovation. Policy and support programmes should develop these practices alongside access to GenAI tools. Originality/value The study distinguishes GenAI capability, application and knowledge modelling within one entrepreneurial model and examines entrepreneurial innovation as a mediating knowledge-conversion pathway linking these dimensions with performance and success.

items.title: Rethinking Continuance Intentions in the AI-Augmented Digital Workplace
items.abstract: As digital technologies become increasingly embedded in organizational processes, understanding the determinants of continued technology usage, particularly in AI-augmented digital workplaces, is essential for optimizing employee engagement and performance. This study evaluates continuance intentions in AI-augmented remote work systems by extending the Expectation Confirmation Model (ECM) with constructs such as perceived enjoyment, trust in technology, self-efficacy, and user satisfaction. Using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) on data from 348 experienced users of digital work platforms, our analysis reveals that trust and perceived enjoyment significantly influence satisfaction, which in turn drives continued usage intentions. Notably, the dynamics of remote work technology adoption diverge from prior information systems continuance models, with enjoyment and psychological assurance playing more prominent roles than traditionally modeled constructs like utility alone. These findings highlight the evolving expectations of knowledge workers in AI-enabled work environments, where user-centric design, intelligent automation, and trustworthy system behaviors are paramount. The study offers actionable insights for system designers and digital transformation leaders seeking to sustain user engagement in an increasingly hybrid and AI-integrated workplace. The results provide important implications for organizations designing or deploying digital collaboration tools.

items.title: Scaffold or Cognitive Crutch? A Two-Level Meta-Analysis of AI Scaffolding Effects on Achievement and Self-Regulated Learning in STEM Education
items.abstract: Background. Artificial intelligence (AI) now mediates much of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) learning, yet adoption has outpaced theory. The tension is whether AI scaffolding relieves cognitive burden or performs the self-regulatory work autonomy requires, and implementation varies too widely for a single average to describe. Objectives. This review estimates the pooled effect of AI scaffolding on STEM achievement and self-regulated learning, tests whether technological paradigm moderates that effect, and asks whether the literature can evaluate learning after support is withdrawn. Methods. Under PRISMA 2020, four platforms searched in October 2026 (spanning 2021–2026) yielded 21,819 records; 13,786 unique records were dual-screened into an 83-record corpus, then 41 extracted cohorts. Each contributes one harmonised contrast (k = 29; N = 3,709), so within-study dependence is structurally absent. Effects were pooled by two-level random-effects meta-analysis fitted with restricted maximum likelihood and Knapp–Hartung adjustment. Results. The pooled effect was Hedges g = 0.8045 (95% CI [0.5469, 1.0621]), with τ² = 0.4410 and I² = 92.78%. The 95% prediction interval [−0.5846, 2.1936] spans zero, and no moderator reached significance. Notably, 27 of 29 cohorts (93.1%) never withdrew support, and none measured unassisted performance after removal. Conclusions. AI scaffolding yields a large but implementation-dependent gain, consistent with extraneous-load offloading rather than cognitive substitution. The decisive finding is the shape of the evidence base: the field measured a human-AI system in assembly and stayed silent on the competence of the human alone. We name this evidentiary void the Autonomy Gap. Keywords: artificial intelligence; self-regulated learning; STEM education; scaffolding fading; cognitive load theory; transfer of responsibility; meta-analysis; evidence synthesis

items.title: Semantic Privilege Collapse: Trust Boundaries and Execution-Level Authorization in Agentic AI Systems
items.abstract: Large language model agents operating within tool-enabled pipelines create opportunities for untrusted content to influence consequential actions. This note introduces semantic privilege collapse as an architectural failure condition in which task data or insufficiently authorized instructions are promoted into effective action authority through model interpretation. The term does not claim discovery of a wholly new vulnerability: it synthesizes the confused-deputy problem, prompt-injection risks, capability-oriented control, and modern agentic authorization requirements. Drawing on OWASP’s 2025 LLM Top 10, OWASP agent-security guidance, Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Simon Willison’s Dual LLM pattern, and Google DeepMind’s CaMeL research, the note distinguishes behavioral resistance to prompt injection from independently enforced execution authorization. It further distinguishes a principal’s standing permissions from task-specific authority and action-specific approval. The central argument is that semantic interpretation is not authorization evidence: protected operations require complete mediation through controls that validate identity, scope, policy, and required approvals independently of model-generated assertions. The analysis recognizes that malicious actions can remain policy-permitted when enforced policies are broader than the intended task. A reference security stack, properties of effective execution authorization, and proposed evaluation criteria are held in a restricted companion edition.

items.title: Simulating Employment Displacement under Partial, Advanced and Near-Full AI and Automation Deployment in Bangladesh's Ready-Made Garment Factories: A Process-Level Model
items.abstract: This paper presents a process-level simulation of employment impacts from artificial intelligence and automation in Bangladesh's ready-made garment (RMG) sector. Using a representative 1,500-worker factory calibrated to recent empirical evidence, three scenarios are modelled: partial automation reflecting current observed trends (approximately 34 per cent reduction), advanced automation combined with AI applications (approximately 58 per cent reduction), and a near-full theoretical maximum (approximately 75 per cent reduction). Results indicate that helpers and lower-skilled operators bear the largest absolute and relative losses, with women accounting for roughly two-thirds of displaced workers across scenarios. Scaling the advanced scenario to sector level produces job losses on the order of 2.3 million, consistent in magnitude with independent forward projections. Technical constraints on fully autonomous sewing of complex garments, combined with potential output growth and new technical roles, moderate absolute employment decline. The findings underscore the urgency of just-transition policies, targeted reskilling, and product upgrading for Bangladesh's largest export industry. KSCCN article, 10 October 2026. items.title: Smart Camera Traps in the Field: A Scoping Review of Architecture and Energy Evidence
items.abstract: Edge Artificial Intelligence (Edge AI) is used in wildlife monitoring to reduce communication demand, support decision-making, and enable energy-aware operation, yet embedded inference alone does not establish whether a system can sustain useful service after installation. This scoping review searched four bibliographic databases through 5 August 2026 and complemented these searches with studies identified from prior work on the topic, identifying 41 eligible English-language papers published from 2021 onward on camera-primary intelligent wildlife systems. The review aimed to assess operational maturity, field-validated operational role, energy evidence, and operational continuity. Full texts were charted and analyzed across sensing, decision-making, communication, response, energy, and continuity. Post-installation evidence exposed triggering, environmental, connectivity, maintenance, and energy-supply constraints not established through non-field evaluation. Field-validated alert delivery did not extend to quantitative validation linking human action to mitigation outcomes, while field activation of physical intervention alone did not establish behavioral or management effectiveness. Energy evidence was even more limited, with limited direct operational electrical measurement, rare main-state characterization, and no complete lifetime energy budget evidence. By separating architectural capability from the evidence supporting its operational realization, the review provides a systems-level basis for interpreting how far reported functions are actually validated. Across the corpus, optimization often shifts constraints among computation, triggering, communication, energy supply, and availability rather than eliminating them. Wildlife Edge AI should therefore be evaluated as a complete field system under application-relevant conditions.

items.title: Socratic, Artifact-Gated Generative AI Scaffolding in a 6E Inquiry Unit: A Clustered Quasi-Experiment in Elementary Students’ Computational Thinking
items.abstract: Open-ended computational thinking (CT) inquiry challenges one teacher to support learners progressing at different rates. This clustered quasi-experiment evaluated TALPer, a generative-AI tutor providing student-initiated, artifact-contingent Socratic prompts during a six-lesson 6E unit. Ten intact Grade 3 classes in Taiwan (N = 229) completed the same curriculum, tasks, teacher, platform, and instructional time. Conditions differed in a bundled scaffolding configuration involving source, delivery modality, initiation, privacy, and artifact requirements. A two-level model controlling for pretest CT estimated an adjusted posttest difference favoring TALPer ( B = 4.05, SE = 1.58, Wald 95% CI [0.94, 7.15], p = .011; sensitivity p = .034; Hedges’ g = 0.52). Class-clustered analyses found no Holm-adjusted difference on any Intrinsic Motivation Inventory subscale; Perceived Choice had the largest positive estimate ( B = 0.27, cluster-adjusted SE = 0.12, 95% CI [−0.02, 0.55], p = .061, pHolm = .306; Hedges’ g = 0.38). The Condition × Pretest interaction was nonsignificant ( B = −0.109, SE = 0.125, 95% CI [-0.354, 0.137], p = .385). Descriptive coding of 101 matched responses showed different distributions of expected and planned AI-use orientations; no inferential transition test was conducted. Findings provide preliminary evidence concerning the bundled intervention but do not isolate component contributions.

items.title: Surveillance, Detection and Therapeutic Innovation in Antimicrobial Resistance in the Age of Polycrisis: From Genomic and Digital Innovation to One Health Integration
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance is increasingly strained by interconnected global crises, i.e., pandemics, climate change, armed conflicts, population mobility, and health inequalities, that disrupt healthcare delivery, diagnostic capacity, and laboratory infrastructure. In parallel, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, whole-genome sequencing, metagenomics, and digital surveillance offer the potential to shift from reactive reporting to predictive intelligence that anticipates resistance threats, although current implementations remain sector-specific, retrospective, and project-funded. Environmental surveillance, particularly wastewater monitoring coupled with genomic epidemiology, provides early warnings at population and ecosystem levels. The future integration of AI across human, animal, and environmental sectors could enable unified One Health intelligence; no such integrated platform is currently operational. This review focuses primarily on bacterial AMR. It examines how global drivers strain surveillance, how genomic, metagenomic, digital, and AI-enabled technologies reshape AMR detection and prediction, and the emerging non-antibiotic therapeutic landscape, including bacteriophage therapy, Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)-based antimicrobials, antimicrobial peptides, microbiota-directed interventions, nanomedicine, host-directed therapies, photodynamic therapy, and vaccines. It then explores how these innovations can be integrated within a One Health framework to support coordinated global preparedness. Addressing the AMR crisis will require not only technological innovation but also equitable implementation, interdisciplinary collaboration, and resilient systems.

items.title: Sustainable AI Governance: A Theoretical Framework for Legal Compliance and Environmental Accountability A Systematic Conceptual Review
items.abstract: The fast increase in artificial intelligence (AI) in vital points in society has created significant governance issues at the interface of environmental sustainability and legal responsibility. Although there is a rich literature on AI ethics, technical safety, and standalone regulatory compliance, a cohesive theoretical framework that encompasses both legal compliance and environmental responsibility conditions under one governance framework have not existed yet, seemingly conspicuously in the literature. The review thus poses the question of how legal compliance requirements and environmental accountability requirements for AI systems can be incorporated in one, theoretically coherent governance architecture, and what are the structural gaps in existing regulatory instruments in this context? This gap is filled in this paper, by introducing the Sustainable AI Governance Framework (SAGF) a conceptual model, three pillars in theory which integrates regulatory coherence, environmental accountability and legal compliance architecture. A systematic conceptual review of studies published in the period 2021–2025 and indexed in Scopus, WoS and PubMed (search on 3–10 March 2026) was carried out after PRISMA 2020. For empirical studies, the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool was used to assess the quality of the studies and for doctrinal and conceptual studies, a five-item checklist was used. To develop the SAGF, 58 articles in sustainability science, environmental law, governance theory and AI regulation were selected fulfilling the inclusion criteria. The article outlines seven key global regulatory tools, seven research gaps (six corpus-derived and one framework-level), and presents a policy roadmap plan that includes mandatory carbon disclosures by AI, legal harmonization across jurisdictions, and tiered organizational standards of compliance. The results have shown that current regulatory frameworks are methodically ineffective in uniting environmental and legal aspects of AI regulation and expose structural gaps, which are inadequately addressed by technical norms and soft-law tools. The paper adds a theoretically sound and practically feasible model to help legislators, regulatory bodies, AI creators, and legal professionals negotiating the twin demands of both sustainable and legally responsible AI use on a globally scale.

items.title: Sustaining Safe Harbors: The Mediating Roles of SARC and Safety Culture in the Relationship Between OHSMS and Safety Performance in the Port Industry: A Case of Korea
items.abstract: The sustainability of global maritime supply chains ultimately depends on the safety of frontline port workers, yet high-risk, multi-stakeholder port operations continue to face persistent occupational hazards that threaten this goal. Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems (OHSMS) serve as a core governance tool for sustainable safety management, but their effectiveness depends not on formal existence alone, but on workers’ cognitive recognition and cultural internalization, particularly under South Korea’s Serious Accidents Punishment Act. This study examined how OHSMS perception is related to safety performance (SP) among port workers, testing the parallel and serial mediating roles of Serious Accident Response Capability (SARC) and Safety Culture (SC) as pathways toward socially sustainable safety outcomes. Cross-sectional survey data from 432 South Korean port workers were analyzed using structural equation modeling. OHSMS perception was positively associated with both SARC and SC, and SC showed the strongest direct association with SP. In the main model, the direct paths from OHSMS and SARC to SP were non-significant, consistent with indirect-only mediation through SC, and the serial pathway (OHSMS → SARC → SC → SP) was significant; however, the SARC → SP path became significant in a common method sensitivity analysis. These cross-sectional results represent associations rather than causal effects. The findings suggest that safety performance in the port sector is associated less with formal regulatory compliance alone than with the internalization of safety practices in a shared safety culture, which is relevant to United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-Being).

items.title: Talent Intelligence dalam Organisasi Modern: Integrasi Data, Teknologi, dan Pengembangan Talenta
items.abstract: The growth of digital technology and artificial intelligence has pushed companies to handle their employees in a more adaptable and data-based way. Talent Intelligence has become a way to combine worker data, technology, analysis, and people factors to help make better decisions in human resources. This study looks at how Talent Intelligence is used in managing people, what role it plays in finding and boosting employee skills, how technology that uses data affects this process, and what things help or stop organizations from using it effectively today. This study uses a Systematic Literature Review method, which includes steps like searching for sources, screening them, selecting the most relevant ones, and then analyzing the content to find themes and patterns. The results show that Talent Intelligence helps companies find out what each person is good at, understand their skills, help them grow and stay with the company, and plan for future work needs by using data from employees, analyzing people data, and applying artificial intelligence. How well it works depends on the quality of the data, the ability to analyze it, how ready the organization is for digital tools, the rules in place to manage it, and the role people play in using it. The main difficulties are biased algorithms, keeping personal information safe, and how technology can't fully understand human feelings and situations. Talent Intelligence connects technology with talent growth to make organizations more flexible and prepared.

items.title: Talent Mobility dalam Ekosistem Digital
items.abstract: Digital transformation has changed the way organizations manage human resources, including in the areas of acquiring, developing, retaining, and mobilizing talent. In this context, talent mobility is no longer limited to employee transfers but also encompasses career mobility, knowledge transfer, competency development, and the adaptation of talent to the organization’s increasingly dynamic needs. This study aims to analyze the development of research on talent mobility within the digital ecosystem and to identify patterns of findings, methodological approaches, and key themes emerging in the literature. The study employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach, involving a systematic process of literature identification, selection, extraction, and synthesis based on predetermined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The results of the study indicate that talent mobility is evolving at the intersection of talent management, digital transformation, competency development, career mobility, artificial intelligence, and digital talent management. The literature also highlights the increasing use of digital technologies in competency mapping, career development, recruitment, training, retention, and talent needs planning. This study contributes by integrating the perspectives of talent mobility and digital transformation and provides a conceptual foundation for organizations to develop adaptive, data-driven talent management systems.

items.title: Task-oriented and relational perceptions of ChatGPT among generation Z students: Implications for higher education and preparation for AI-enabled work
items.abstract: Generative AI is becoming embedded in higher education and knowledge work, yet students may assign different forms of usefulness to conversational AI. This study examines how Generation Z students perceive the current and potential usefulness of ChatGPT across seven functional roles. Data were collected from April to June 2024 through an online survey of 409 students from different disciplines at multiple Polish higher education institutions using a geographically diversified, non-probability convenience sampling strategy. Medians, quartiles, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used to analyse ordinal responses. Task-oriented roles, particularly information search and idea generation, were rated more highly than relational roles, while all roles received higher ratings for potential than for current usefulness. By integrating multiple roles within task-oriented and relational dimensions, the study extends role-based understanding of student-AI interaction. The findings suggest implications for AI literacy and responsible human-AI collaboration in higher education, while remaining limited to students’ perceptions.

items.title: The cognitive cost of artificial intelligence on ageing workforce: Analyzing age-related effects on mental workload and task performance in computer-based environment
items.abstract: Background The current world demographic reality necessitates a critical re-evaluation of how technological tools, specifically those powered by artificial intelligence (AI), interact with the varying cognitive profiles of a ageing workforce. Objectives The objective of this study is to evaluate the spatial distribution of mental workload and objective task performance across AI-assisted and non-AI-assisted conditions in a computer-based environment. Method An experimental study involving 30 older workers compared standardized office tasks under non-AI-assisted (Segment A) and AI-assisted (Segment B) conditions. Mental workload was assessed using NASA-TLX, Heart Rate Variability (HRV), and EEG-based Beta-Alpha Ratios (BAR) across frontal (F3, F4), parietal (P3, P4), and occipital (O1, O2) regions. Performance in document preparation (Task 1) and arithmetic operations (Task 2) was evaluated using percentage-based accuracy, efficiency, and overall performance scores. Result AI intervention improved overall task performance but was accompanied by an apparent performance–workload paradox, whereby enhanced output coincided with increased neurophysiological and systemic strain. Descriptively, NASA-TLX Overall Perceived Workload decreased from 54.05 to 44.91 during complex tasks, while HRV declined by 48.68% in Task 1, indicating acute autonomic strain. EEG revealed increased BAR in the frontal (F3: 29.2%), parietal (P3), and occipital (O1) regions, suggesting heightened attentional and sensory demands associated with monitoring and verifying AI-generated suggestions. Conclusion AI redistributes rather than eliminates workload, increasing executive verification and visual monitoring demands. items.title: The Consulting Firm Reconstituted: Building for Mixed Human-AI Delivery
items.abstract: Professional services firms moved AI-assisted delivery from pilot to production between 2024 and 2026. This paper takes up five questions that follow. What does a firm sell once clients can license the same models? Who answers for an error that passes through five agents? Does a validator role build judgment, or only train the next model? What separates a governed AI deliverable from one that fails its own citations? And what can a new hire expect three years out? The paper treats commercial model, operating design, and behavioral incentives as one design problem. Its main mechanisms are an Emergency Override Protocol that makes declaring a suspension cheaper than hiding one; a paired metric that pays partners for keeping human capability only when delivery efficiency also holds; a rotating Challenger role grounded in vigilance research; an experience-portfolio talent model built around two to three years of tenure and an alumni network; and a two-tier operating model for data-residency regimes, with Saudi Arabia as the worked case. The paper argues that the firm's lasting advantages are its independence from the client's frame, accountability that a regulator can reach, and a data feedback loop competitors cannot buy. Working paper, not peer reviewed. The views expressed in this paper are the author's own and do not represent the position of his employer or any of its member firms.

items.title: The Effectiveness of Primary and Secondary Radar in the Malaysian Air Defence Mechanism
items.abstract: Radar surveillance constitutes a critical component of modern air-defence systems, enabling states to detect, identify, track and respond to aerial activities. This capability is particularly important for Malaysia due to its geographical separation, extensive maritime approaches, large airspace and increasing exposure to foreign military aircraft, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and unidentified aerial activities. Primary Surveillance Radar (PSR) and Secondary Surveillance Radar (SSR) perform complementary functions. PSR independently detects airborne objects through reflected electromagnetic signals without target cooperation. SSR relies on aircraft transponders to provide identification and other flight information. This distinction is significant for national air defence because non-cooperative targets may not provide information required by SSR. This study examines the effectiveness of PSR and SSR within Malaysia’s air-defence mechanism through qualitative documentary and case study analysis of international standards, Malaysian aviation policies, surveillance infrastructure, parliamentary records, official defence documents and selected airspace incidents. The findings indicate that Malaysia possesses a credible and increasingly modern surveillance foundation comprising PSR, SSR, Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) and dedicated military radar capabilities. However, effectiveness remains constrained by uneven geographical coverage, equipment availability, low-altitude surveillance challenges, dependence on cooperative systems and fragmented civil-military surveillance functions. The study argues that Malaysia’s challenge extends beyond radar acquisition to the incomplete integration of sensors, surveillance data, institutional responsibilities, and decision-making processes. A layered national air-surveillance architecture integrating PSR, SSR, ADS-B, long-range military radar and complementary sensors within a common operational picture is therefore essential to strengthen situational awareness, response time, and the protection of national sovereignty and territorial integrity.

items.title: The Era of Super intelligence (SI) and the Indian Education System: Challenges, Opportunities, and Future Directions
items.abstract: This research paper presents a serious and comprehensive analysis of how the emerging and rapidly changing era of 'Super intelligence' (SI) is fundamentally transforming the fabric of global and Indian society. In the history of modern technological revolutions, this turning point is the most unprecedented, where the traditional boundaries of artificial intelligence have been shattered and intellectual capacity is moving far beyond the scope of human control. Basic sectors such as education, health, employment, and industries are being affected the most by this technological leap. Focusing on these broad, complex, and far-reaching effects, this research paper closely examines the current preparedness of the Indian education system, the emerging trends of the younger generation, the serious challenges encountered along the way, and a comparative study with the foreign perspective of developed countries. In the next phase of the study, this research explores ideological paths to save Indian identity, culture, and originality amidst globalization and the blind race of technology. For this, the provisions of the National Education Policy (NEP 2020), modern technological requirements, and the support of our rich Indian philosophical tradition and 'Indian Knowledge Systems' (IKS) have been made the basis. The main objective of the research is to emphasize that in this race for the future, only technical proficiency is not enough; rather, the inclusion of moral values, character-building, and human sensitivities is equally essential. Finally, this research paper presents practical and policy suggestions to make the future direction robust, inclusive, self-reliant, and balanced, so that this torrential era of super intelligence does not become a cause of destruction for the Indian education system and society, but rather proves to be a great boon. This study will serve as an important document for policy-makers, academicians, and researchers in preparing the framework for the future.

items.title: The Extractive Imperative Thesis in AI: Instrumental Training via Soft Hacking for Adversarial Scenario Harvesting in Real Incidents
items.abstract: This working paper poses a methodological alternative to the anthropomorphicnarrative of 'rogue machines' in Artificial Intelligence safety and alignment. It examines the possibility that certain training and evaluation environments, by combining operational restriction conditions with rigid optimization goals, induce secondary rule evasion behaviors ('soft hacking'). Furthermore, it is postulated that the systematic harvesting of these adversarial scenarios could serve to equip second-generation safety monitors with long-range trajectory prediction capabilities and complex cognitive precursor detection, rather than relying solely on the reactive analysis of isolated actions. This paper formalizes this line of research by defining the concept of the extractive imperative as an analytical risk hypothesis, structuring layers of empirical evidence, establishing rigorous operational definitions, and proposing a replicable experimental protocol alongside explicit refutation criteria. Additionally, the concept of liability laundering is addressed as a legal-organizational risk hypothesis, explicitly separating technical design, economic incentives, internal knowledge, intent, and legal liability.

items.title: The Futuristic Imagination Sprawl: Charting Concepts vs. Social Realities
items.abstract: This introductory article provides the theoretical framing for the Japanese Studies special issue, ‘Japanese Technofutures – Imaginaries, Narratives, Social Realities’. The contributions focus on Japan as a primary site for technofuturistic imaginations, driven by both external techno-orientalist attributions and deeply internalized self-conceptualizations. Yet, these technological promises frequently present a paradox: they commodify the future while masking persistent social and structural inequalities in the present. Acknowledging that both area studies and science and technology studies (STS) discursively construct their respective subjects, this introduction bridges the two fields by charting the conceptual landscape of the ‘futuristic imagination sprawl’. It demonstrates that differentiating Sheila Jasanoff’s sociotechnical imaginaries from adjacent concepts enriches our investigation of future-oriented imaginations with greater clarity and precision. Grounded in this framework, the special issue’s case studies examine how Japanese technofutures are envisioned, institutionalized, translated, and contested from the 1960s to the present.

items.title: The HCI-H Model: Development of a Context-Sensitive Mathematical Framework for Prospective Healthcare Procedure Risk Assessment and Preventive Decision Support
items.abstract: This project proposes the development of the HCI-H Model, a multidimensional mathematical framework designed to assess the risk of harm associated with healthcare procedures according to local clinical and organizational conditions. The model integrates human factors, organizational risks, punitive culture, professional hierarchy, humanization of care, patient vulnerability, artificial intelligence-related risks, clinical decision-making, and the unjustified dismissal of safety warnings. Risk management and organizational resilience are incorporated as protective factors. The proposed mathematical equation aims to generate a relative risk score that may support the prospective identification of unsafe conditions and inform decisions regarding additional preventive measures, supervision, and safety barriers. This research protocol presents the theoretical foundations, mathematical formulation, and proposed methods for examining the model's consistency, sensitivity, and applicability across healthcare settings. The HCI-H Model is currently a theoretical framework under development. Its mathematical assumptions, predictive performance, and clinical utility require further empirical validation before implementation as a clinical decision-support tool.

items.title: The impact of generative artificial intelligence on clinical decision-making and patient safety: A narrative review
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI), in the form of large language models (LLMs), has entered clinical practice faster than the evidence on how it changes clinical decisions could be produced. The relevant question is therefore no longer whether these models hold medical knowledge, but whether their use makes clinicians' decisions better and patients' care safer. This narrative review examines the evidence on the impact of generative AI on clinical decision-making and patient safety. In evaluations of encoded knowledge, a medically aligned model gave answers that agreed with scientific consensus in 92.6% of cases, against 92.9% for clinicians. In diagnostic reasoning, a model optimized for diagnosis outperformed unassisted clinicians on challenging cases and improved the differential diagnoses of the clinicians who used it, whereas a randomized trial of a general-purpose chatbot found no significant improvement in physicians' diagnostic reasoning, although the model alone outperformed both physician groups. In management reasoning, physicians assisted by GPT-4 scored 6.5 percentage points higher than those using conventional resources. When tested on real patient data in a simulated clinical workflow, however, LLMs diagnosed less accurately than physicians, did not follow guidelines and were sensitive to the order and quantity of information. The safety literature identifies four recurrent hazards: fabricated content, with hallucination rates of 50% to 82% when prompts contained a false clinical detail; misjudgement of clinical acuity, with drafted patient messages judged to pose a risk of severe harm in 7.1% of assessments; automation bias, by which clinicians adopt the model's assessment in place of their own; and the reproduction of racial and gender stereotypes. Only about 5% of published evaluations used real patient care data. Taken together, the evidence supports generative AI as a supervised aid to clinical reasoning rather than as an autonomous decision-maker, and indicates that its safety depends as much on the design of the human–AI interaction as on the accuracy of the model. Practical safeguards for clinical use are also reviewed.
